confidence_notes: Restaurant meal, coffee and beer prices come from searches of cost-of-living aggregators (Livingcost, CityCost, Oysterlist, Nomad Watch). These sources broadly agree: an inexpensive meal is about $7-8, a cappuccino about $2.9-3.2, a pub beer about $2.8 (Nomad Watch is higher at $5), and a mid-range dinner for two about $33-35. I set the beer anchor a little above the aggregator figure because a typical izakaya draft costs about 500-600 yen. Happy-hour deals of 99-199 yen were left out because they are promotions. I raised the mid-range meal slightly to cover three courses. I found no aggregated prices for cocktails or wine by the glass. Those two anchors are based on their usual price relationship to beer in regional Japanese izakaya and bars, which makes them less certain. The accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge of a regional Japanese city with modest tourism (Dogo Onsen, Matsuyama Castle). I did not search for accommodation prices or look at live listings. July summer demand and movement in the yen exchange rate add uncertainty to all USD figures.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with similar regional cities in western Japan, such as Okayama, Takamatsu and Kochi. Prices there run below Tokyo and Osaka, especially for business hotels and izakaya dining.
